title: Efficient Data Storage
subtitle: Store for unpredictable questions and fresh answers
summary: Pip needs a new tenant-build comparison during an incident. Storage tuned only for prepared queries cannot help. Event-level attributes, bounded time scans, and selective column reads preserve investigative flexibility while controlling cost.

concepts.title: The workload determines the design
concepts.body: Pip asks about a tenant-build combination nobody previously queried. Investigation needs new groupings over retained event attributes, including fresh arrivals. Prepared-query optimization alone may make unfamiliar questions slow or impossible. Pip also checks fault tolerance because the store must help verify changes while production is under stress.

concepts.title: Time segments bound the scan
concepts.body: Pip queries a narrow incident window in Retriever. Append-only segments record their oldest and newest event timestamps so nonoverlapping segments can be skipped. Events need not arrive in exact timestamp order. Pip avoids mixing very old backfill broadly with fresh events, which widens ranges and increases later scans.

concepts.title: Columns reduce unnecessary reads
concepts.body: Pip groups latency by build without reading every request header. Column storage reads filtered, grouped, and returned fields within relevant segments. Sparse and repeated values can compress efficiently. Pip balances fast analytical scans against the extra work needed to reconstruct full events and traces.

concepts.title: Avoid preselecting every future question
concepts.body: Pip considers making every request ID a metric label. Unique request-like values create new series instead of reusable aggregate combinations. The chapter favors retained events and efficient reads without preselecting or specially indexing every future dimension. Pip preserves flexibility for the next unfamiliar question.

misconceptions.claim: Time partitioning requires perfectly ordered event arrival.
misconceptions.correction: Segment metadata can track timestamp ranges while writes remain append-only; late data affects scan efficiency.

misconceptions.claim: Retriever is presented as the only valid observability database design.
misconceptions.correction: It is a concrete reference architecture used to explain trade-offs and functional requirements.

scenario.title: Backfill slows live investigation
scenario.context: A pipeline mixes week-old spans with current events, and narrow recent-time queries now scan many segments.

options.label: Examine segment ranges and separate backfill handling
options.benefit: Can restore useful time pruning while retaining historical data.
options.consequence: Recent queries may scan fewer irrelevant segments once backfill is organized appropriately.

options.label: Increase query workers immediately
options.benefit: May reduce latency by adding capacity.
options.cost: Can mask widening scan ranges and raise operating cost.
options.consequence: The same poorly pruned queries consume a larger worker fleet.

scenario.debrief: Understand whether the scan is large because of data organization before treating it only as a capacity problem.

quiz.question: What is a likely effect of mixing very old backfill into every fresh segment?
options: Narrower timestamp bounds because segments are grouped by arrival order
More segments overlap a typical query window
No read impact because timestamp ranges are irrelevant once files are immutable
quiz.explanation: Wider segment bounds weaken time-based pruning even when ingestion remains valid.

quiz.question: Why does column storage help a query using only three of many fields?
options: It retrieves each full row before discarding the unused fields
It can skip the time filter whenever columns are compressed
It can avoid reading unrelated columns
quiz.explanation: Reading only required fields reduces the analytical scan workload.

quiz.question: Why is a request ID an awkward traditional metric label?
options: It creates many new label combinations with little reuse
The identifier forces all dimensions to be stored in a single numeric value
It improves series reuse because each request has an exact label
quiz.explanation: High uniqueness undermines the amortization that makes reused time series efficient.
